episodes.157521: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damage wind gusts in portions of eastern West Virginia and western Maryland.
episodes.157526: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the mid afternoon hours in northwest moving into north central Alabama.  A couple of the thunderstorms produced tree damage and small hail.
episodes.157593: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damage wind gusts in portions of eastern West Virginia and western Maryland.
episodes.157720: After several days of moist, low-level easterly flow across eastern New Mexico, that trend finally diminished as winds across the area became more variable. With an area of high pressure building over the Rockies, drier air began to filter into the area which lessened storm coverage on June 1, 2021. Still, enough moisture and instability continued to allow for thunderstorms with isolated severe thunderstorms for areas along and east of the central mountain chain. The strongest thunderstorms for the day were located across south central and east central New Mexico where nickel to quarter size hail was reported. Minor home damage was also reported in Dilia with the large hail.
episodes.157721: With drier air continuing to filter into the area and moist low-level return flow becoming less organized, the severe weather threat continued to diminish on June 2, 2021. However, there still remained enough atmospheric ingredients to produce another round of thunderstorm activity mainly focused along and east of the central mountain chain. Multiple funnel clouds were spotted in Mora County with even one brief landspout tornado reported near Rainsville. These thunderstorms also produced very strong winds with the strongest thunderstorm wind gust of 67 mph measured in Tucumcari.
episodes.157953: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the South Plains and Rolling Plains on the afternoon of the first in a moderately unstable environment ahead of an approaching short wave. These storms remained sub-severe producing only penny size hail at McAdoo (Dickens County).
episodes.157964: Early in the morning on the second, a mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved southeastward out of the Texas Panhandle into the South Plains. This MCS maintained its intensity as it reached the Rolling Plains and began to develop a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) on the north side of a bowing line segment. As this occurred, a couple of severe thunderstorm wind gusts were observed by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
episodes.158748: A severe thunderstorm clipped far southern Tripp County and produced wind gusts to 60 mph south of Millboro.
episodes.158965: Severe thunderstorms resulted in 1-inch hail and damaging winds across the Greater Houston Area.
episodes.158984: Numerous showers and thunderstorms occurred along a stationary front that extended from the Great Lakes southward across the lower Mississippi Valley. Locally excessive rainfall produced extensive road flooding in Calloway County.
episodes.159121: Through the first week of June, slow moving storm systems aloft, clouds, and areas of rain kept temperatures down. There was enough rain to cover Highway 67 with water near Donaldson (Hot Spring County) on the 1st. In the twenty four hour period ending at 700 am CDT on the 2nd, two to three inches of rain dumped at Antoine (Pike County), Jessieville (Garland County), and Murfreesboro (Pike County).
episodes.159146: Heavy rain in early June brought flooding to several rivers in central and northeast Arkansas.
episodes.159456: There was an upper level trough that was impacting West Texas. Modest instability and wind shear were across the area. These conditions allowed for thunderstorms with hail to develop in the Permian Basin.
episodes.159457: An upper level trough was impacting West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. Instability and wind shear were fairly high across the area. There was an outflow boundary in the Permian Basin from thunderstorms during the morning hours. An upper level disturbance was also moving southeast across West Texas. These conditions lead to thunderstorms that developed across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico that produced hail and strong winds.
episodes.159643: An isolated supercell developed along a residual outflow boundary and produced large hail across southwest Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 2nd.
episodes.160023: A line of thunderstorms moved through the Jackson Metropolitan area on the afternoon of June 2nd, producing strong gusty winds.  One of the storms became severe and produced a microburst at the Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers Airport.
episodes.160093: A warm front produced thunderstorms that developed a couple tornadoes.
episodes.160186: A closed upper low was situated over Oklahoma while the warm sector destabilized across the Mid-South during the afternoon hours of June 2, 2021. A weak surface pressure trough pushing through West Tennessee and Northeast Mississippi helped to ignite slow-moving storms during the afternoon and into the evening. There were a few severe weather reports along with isolated flash flooding.
episodes.160188: A closed upper low was situated over Oklahoma while the warm sector destabilized across the Mid-South during the afternoon hours of June 2, 2021. A weak surface pressure trough pushing through West Tennessee and Northeast Mississippi helped to ignite slow-moving storms during the afternoon and into the evening. There were a few severe weather reports along with isolated flash flooding.
episodes.160269: A few thunderstorms formed across east Colorado in the evening hours. Storms were generally strong/sub-severe, but one storm was able to produce a brief landspout tornado.
episodes.160298: Strong afternoon instability resulted in isolated to scattered thunderstorms. A few storms were severe across the Big Country and Concho Valley.
episodes.160561: The combination of a warm front and sea breeze moving across Eastern North Carolina led to numerous showers along with a few thunderstorms on the afternoon of June 2nd.  One thunderstorm produced an EF1 tornado in Duplin County.

events.narrative: Water covered Highway 67 and Front Street in Donaldson.

A brief, unexpected landspout tornado developed between Bethune, CO and Interstate 70. No damage was reported with this tornado. This was reported via emergency management, law enforcement, storm chasers, NWS Employees, and the general public.
Wind gusts were estimated at 60 mph.

Multiple sources in Dilia reported nickel to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area. One resident of Dilia reported that the hail broke their skylight. Damages are estimated for the loss of the skylight.
Heavy rain brought flooding to the Black River at Black Rock in early June 2021.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 59 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Paducah measured a wind gust to 59 mph.
A brief landspout tornado occurred over an open field near Highway 158 west of Luxora.
A brief landspout tornado was spotted near Rainsville. No damage was reported.
A social media report relayed by broadcast media indicated that two trees were knocked down in Anderson. Time estimated by radar.

An EF-1 tornado touched down 1.8 miles SW of the town of|Teachey, NC over a small farm. A metal shed was destroyed before lofting and destroying|an unanchored trailer. Parts of metal roofs of multiple small farm outbuildings were also|peeled or torn off. One metal roof landed on an unoccupied vehicle. The tornado then|crossed over Cornwallis Rd where it snapped the trunks of three large pine trees and|toppled an unanchored shed. The tornado proceeded 1 mile or so over a field into an |inaccessible wooded area, potentially lifting, before dropping over the town of Teachey, |knocking down multiple trees before lifting over Ramsey St.  Local emergency |management received multiple reports of this tornado being sighted in town.

An apparent microburst produced severe wind gusts over the span of a few minutes at the KJAN ASOS site at Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers Airport.  The initial gust of 58 mph out of the south-southwest was followed by a peak gust of 74 mph out of the south-southwest.
Half-dollar size hail fell along Cedar Grove Church Road and Sawmill Road.
Quarter size hail fell along Highway 641 north of Camden.
Numerous rural county roads were either flooded or completely washed out from near Almo to Dexter and surrounding areas.

The tornado formed close to Old Highway 74 just east of Evergreen|where it damaged a metal hog structure. The tornado then moved|northeast where it snapped one small tree and damaged a corn|field. It then lifted before touching down again near another hog|farm where more appreciable damage was observed. One structure in|this complex observed roof collapse and other damage. Two hogs|also perished in this vicinity. The other hog structures in the|complex had a few metal roof panels pulled off. Minor tree damage|occurred just northeast of the hog farm before the tornado lifted|near Silver Spoon Road.
A tree was knocked down off of Cowford Road in Athens. Time estimated by radar.
A tree was knocked down east of downtown Athens. Time estimated by radar.
A storm chaser reported golf ball size hail at the I-20/US 84 spilt east of Roscoe.
There were multiple reports of trees and wires blown down between Westernport and McCoole.

There were multiple reports of trees and wires blown down in Keyser, including a tree down in the 300 block of WV-46 West Piedmont Street, a large tree and power lines down on a house in the 100 block of Front Street, and a tree down near the intersection of WV-46 Carroll Avenue and Vernon Street.
The West Texas Mesonet site reported a wind gust of 66 mph.
A thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust near Goldsmith.
There were reports of a couple of trees blown down in the Old Town area.
Strong thunderstorm outflow produced a 67 mph wind gust at the Tucumcari airport.
A television news crew reported quarter to dime sized hail near New Caney.
Numerous trees were downed near and around Tavola Elementary School.
